content.thinking:
I'm tracing the incident timeline: the monthly-spend-feature flag flipped on at 01:23:00Z, triggering evaluation spikes across G971b and Gce95, followed by a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py at line 47 persisting from 01:23 to 01:31. I'm now piecing together what the second piece of evidence shows.

The flag was switched off at 01:29:59Z, but Gce95 continued showing "on" evaluations through 01:31 — meaning the revert never actually reached the service, which is why the mitigation looked refuted and the flag got switched back on at T21. So the fix isn't to question the flag as root cause, but to re-apply the off-switch in a way that actually propagates to the service and verify via logs that monthly-spend-feature shows off evaluations and the ZeroDivisionError stops.

Building out the causal chain now: shoppers hit failed account pages (G5309, Gbac1 error rate spiking to 35%), caused by a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, triggered by the monthly-spend-feature flag being switched on at 01:23:00 by an admin (P1, G971b, Gce95). I'm checking whether a deploy could be the real cause instead of the flag — T9 shows only one production change, T10 shows all replicas converged on a single revision — but it's unclear if deploys are formally ruled out by the record.

I can confirm no deploy occurred before the onset since the change events only recorded the flag toggle (T8, T9, P1), and metrics were healthy at baseline 0.9% error rate before 01:23 with the flag off (T5, G7e5d, Gad41), reinforcing that the flag switch is the sole precipitating change.

The ClientDisconnected errors from G46bc (00:53-01:23) look like pre-existing baseline noise, since they occurred at the same low rate before onset per Gbac1's typical 1% figure, so I'll rule those out as unrelated to the incident.

Tracing the actual mechanism: per F1, the monthly average function divides by the count of this-month purchases, which is zero for shoppers who bought before but not this month, and the flag routes exactly these shoppers into that path — this matches G5309's line 47. Since this rests only on F1 with no supporting S or D row, I need to flag that this cause rests on an unrun reading, though it does reach an actual root cause: a missing zero-guard in the division logic, with a contributing factor being the apparent lack of test coverage for the empty-month case before the flag was enabled.

Stepping back to the "don't stop at a person" principle — the admin flipped the flag, but harm occurred because the code path was faulty, and also because the rollout went from off to fully-on across all 200 evaluations within about a minute (per G971b) rather than being staged and gated on error rate, which would have limited the blast radius.

This gives me a contributing factor: no test exercised the monthly-spend path for a no-purchase shopper before the flag could go live, since the existing helper treated it as an ordinary case. I need to check whether my proposed fix item — requiring flag-gated paths to have tests against ordinary account shapes before enabling in production — actually addresses this gap, since the existing AI-1 item seems to only cover the fault the tests already catch, not the missing check itself.

I notice C2 reports the Argus switch-off at 01:29:14, conflicting with P2's 01:29:59 — I should defer to the record. Looking at Gce95's logs through 01:31, evaluations stayed "on" for 8 straight minutes despite the flag being off from 01:29:59, suggesting possible caching, though I shouldn't speculate without more evidence.

CF-3: nobody paged since the alert wasn't linked to an on-call incident — this is a condition of the alert routing config that held before the incident.

CF-4: the flag rolled to all traffic within a minute with no staged rollout. For action items, I'm drafting prevention steps — requiring flag-gated tests to pass with the flag on for ordinary account shapes (like shoppers with no purchases) addresses CF-1, and I still need to work out why io-shop's rollout skipped staging.

Continuing: fixing how the service receives flag changes from the provider mitigates CF-2, alongside detecting when evaluated flag values diverge from the provider's for too long. Routing HighErrorRate on io-shop to on-call paging handles CF-3, and rolling flag changes out in stages that auto-halt on rising error rates addresses CF-4.

For stopping the actual harm, I need to re-disable monthly-spend-feature in a way that actually reaches io-shop this time, then confirm the service logs show the flag off during evaluations, the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 stops occurring, and the error rate returns to its earlier baseline.

For the still-at-risk note, I'll phrase it as: with the flag back on and the division-by-zero bug still present, account pages likely keep failing for shoppers with no purchases this month, since the earlier attempt to flip the flag off at the provider wasn't confirmed to actually reach the service. For the symptom summary, I'll keep it concise — something like "account pages failed for a large share of shoppers."

For the root cause, I'm tracing it to the monthly-average-spend function dividing a shopper's spend by their purchase count with no zero-guard, which throws a ZeroDivisionError at that specific line when a shopper hasn't purchased this month, and enabling the monthly-spend feature routed those shoppers through that code path. I need to reference the exact line number from the error trace as its own labeled figure rather than treating it as plain text.

What went well: Argus quickly tied the onset to the flag change after the alert fired, and mitigation correctly verified the revert rather than assuming it worked, re-flipping the flag when it didn't help. Code-Fix also moved fast, opening a draft PR (#390) with a proposed fix and tests shortly after the alert.

What went wrong: the revert verdict was marked as refuting the candidate flag even though the logs showed the service never actually picked up the change, so the test didn't really exercise the hypothesis — restoring the flag just put the system back in its faulty state. That flawed verdict then propagated, causing the second investigation's candidate to also get marked refuted before Argus moved to fixing.

I'm also flagging that nobody was paged despite the incident conditions being met — I'll keep this as its own CF item rather than folding it into went_wrong, since it's really about the paging configuration holding before the incident.

For the "got lucky" category, the fact that only shoppers with empty this-month purchase lists were affected seems more like a bounded fault than luck, so I'll leave that section empty. On assumptions, I'm noting that the empty-purchases mechanism and its interpretation comes from Code-Fix's reading of the source.

I still need to pin down why the flag-off state never reached the service — the logs only show it evaluating "on" after P2 without explaining the gap — and I'm assuming deploy records showing no matching revision name is itself meaningful here. I'm also assuming the failing request line in the logs matches the file/line Code-Fix identified, based on them lining up exactly.

For detection, I'll just note the alert fired without getting into timing details. For the causal chain, I'm framing it as: the admin switched on the monthly-spend-feature flag at P1.1, and from that moment the service began evaluating it as on, citing P1, G971b, and Gce95, while ruling out T8/T9 deploys as a cause since there's no healthy baseline measurement beforehand.

Now I'm checking the second investigation's two changes (P1 and P2) and noting that replica revision state is tied to when it was read — ruling out an in-progress rollout since all replicas showed one revision at T10.1. Then I'm building the chain: those requests triggered a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code starting right when the flag flipped on, and shoppers' account pages failed as the error rate spiked well above typical levels, citing Gbac1, AL1, and related timestamps.

Next I trace that the failure originated because the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on by an admin, causing the service to evaluate the flag on for an increasing share and then all of its evaluations, whereas before it was off and pages rendered fine — citing P1, G971b, Gce95, G7e5d, and G7e5d, with some entries ruled out along the way.

For CF-2, I note that Argus's revert, had it reached the service, would likely have removed the failing path and shortened the incident, rather than being judged unhelpful and reinstated. For CF-1, I identify that no test existed covering the monthly-spend-feature path for a shopper with zero purchases this month before the flag was enabled.

I'm compiling the "went well" items — alerts firing correctly and the mitigation agent watching the situation — alongside a "went wrong" item about Argus moving to FIXING without explanation despite the flag still evaluating as on. I'm also considering a process improvement: the mitigation verdict check should confirm a revert actually reached the service before judging the candidate refuted, though that falls outside the strict CF framework so I'll include it with an empty answer set. Now I'm drafting the final write-up, making sure to avoid raw numbers in the prose.

action_items.item: Require that the service's tests run and pass with a feature flag on before that flag can be switched on in production, covering ordinary account shapes such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after the provider switched it off, and fix how flag changes reach the service.
Alert when the value io-shop evaluates for a flag stays different from the value the provider holds.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.
Roll out flag changes on io-shop in stages: hold at a small share of traffic first, and stop the rollout automatically when the error rate rises.
Make the Mitigation Agent check that a flag revert has reached the service's own evaluations before it judges the candidate refuted.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages failed. The account page error rate, which was typically {Gbac1.6}, reached {Gbac1.5}. The service's share of requests that failed went from {errors_before} before the onset to an average of {errors_while_broken} while it was broken.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors start in the minute of the onset and do not appear in the logs before it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. The production change events read for the day before the onset held only the flag switch, and no deploys came back.
A rollout still in progress. When read at {T10.1}, all replicas ran the same revision.
Shoppers closing their connections. Those ClientDisconnected errors were logged from before the onset, while the account page error rate sat at its usual level, and they stop at the onset.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. In that same minute the service evaluated the flag as on for some of its evaluations, and from the next minute for all of them. Before the switch the service evaluated the flag as off and account pages rendered normally.

With the flag on, the account page divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises at line {F1.1}, the line the incident's log names.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a setting that added a new monthly spending summary to shoppers' account pages, and that summary likely divides by the number of purchases a shopper has made this month, so it breaks for anyone who has not bought anything yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag could be switched on in production, no test was seen that ran the monthly-spend-feature path for a shopper with no purchases this month. Code-Fix's reading says the cases it added would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Switching monthly-spend-feature off at the provider did not reach the service. After Argus switched it off at {P2.1}, the service still logged every evaluation of the flag as on.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The revert would have taken the failing path out of use at the service and shortened the incident, instead of being judged not to help and put back.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been on the incident while it ran and could have seen that the service still evaluated the flag as on after the revert.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for every evaluation within about a minute, and no staged rollout was seen that would stop it if errors rose.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failure before the rollout stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well: The Investigator Agent formed a candidate naming the monthly-spend-feature switch {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent reverted the flag {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service itself rather than assuming the revert had worked, and put the flag back when the service stayed at the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request with a proposed fix and tests {T36.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The revert was judged refuted even though the logs showed the service still evaluating the flag as on after it was switched off. The revert never reached the service, so the verdict did not test the candidate.

In the second investigation the candidate itself noted that the flag still showed as on, yet it was marked refuted as tested for the first candidate. Argus then moved to FIXING saying no explanation was left to try, rather than following up on why the revert had not reached the service.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out a shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing this month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and nothing guards against that number being zero. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on and the division still in the code, account pages could keep failing, likely for shoppers with no purchases this month, and switching the flag off at the provider was not seen to stop the service evaluating it as on.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again in a way that reaches io-shop. Then confirm at the service that its logs show the flag evaluated as off, that the ZeroDivisionError lines from src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop, and that the error rate falls back to near {errors_before}.
